obligations.note: payments.py#release now returns the stored release only if it is under 1 day old; after that it skips nothing (approvals persist, status is not checked, releases has no uniqueness constraint) and calls _send_disbursement again, so a replayed instruction sends a second disbursement.

Ledger entry ACR-0403 (PAY-2 trace on e5bf646) covers payments.py#release, whose behaviour this change alters, so it has lapsed; no valid replacement evidence exists, and the only fresh signal, the sample control test, never advances the clock past the new window.

Ticket CHG-25827 is a standard ticket approved by Erik Brandt (change_manager) on 2026-09-28, before the change was opened on 2026-09-30; its component payments.payments covers the only touched path, apps/baseline-payments/payments/payments.py.
code_review approval by sofia.santos@fernbrook.example, a change_approver for payments and a different person from the author Jonah Weiss according to the directory.
The approval names head commit d6f3a18, the change's only commit.

The recorded CI run on head d6f3a18 succeeded with 172 tests, 0 failures and 0 skips, including the registered PAY-2 control test test_sampled_release_is_idempotent (sample). A local rerun was not possible because pytest is not installed.
payments.py maps to payments.payments, which is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls data, control tests, CI) are touched, so no control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and emergency is false, so no PIR is due.
The change relies on no exception, and the register has none for PAY-2 or payments.payments, so nothing excuses the PAY-2 deviation.

summary: The change limits release idempotency to a one-day window, so replaying a payment instruction after 24 hours sends a second disbursement to core banking, which refutes PAY-2. The prior PAY-2 evidence (ACR-0403) lapsed with the change and was not replaced; the sample control test passes only because it never moves the clock. The process records (ticket, independent review, approval on head, CI on head) are in order, but a refuted critical product obligation requires rejection.
